key_evidence: On 2 September 2026 the NZ Government released the statutory Crown Review into the 4 February 2026 Moa Point wastewater plant failure. It found the event was not caused by a single decision but by longstanding weaknesses in governance, accountability, asset management, risk management and infrastructure resilience.

The review found Wellington City Council, as plant owner and consent holder, 'remained ultimately accountable', yet relied on Wellington Water's notifications rather than its own standards (ODT). RNZ reports 'no single organisation acted as though it was in charge'.
The Crown Review Team was appointed on 12 March 2026 by the Minister of Local Government under ss 255(3) and 258 of the Local Government Act 2002 (NZ Gazette, tier 5).

Mayor Andrew Little apologised and said under-performance 'was seen as normal'. The acting chief executive said the council 'should have done better' and announced a new role to monitor Tiaki Wai. This is credited: AB1 held at 5, AB2 at 4.
Five subdimensions move down on this evidence (A5, AC4, S2, AB4, I4). Any one of A5, AC4, S2 or I4 alone takes the placeholder below the Exemplary line (79.8); AB4 alone does not (81.8).

approval_note: Founder approved in-session on 2026-09-16 ("approve all and fix all"), after the public briefing and the founder packet disclosed that about 8.0 of the 11.7 points is the integration-premium cliff (RISK-019) rather than additional conduct. Recorded by the coordinator on the founder's explicit written instruction; nothing in the repository can mechanically verify that provenance (RISK-021). The assessor's recommendation and notes are unchanged.
notes: Filed under BOTH triggers: magnitude (-11.7) and band crossing (Exemplary to Established). First individual assessment of a never-assessed placeholder, so about -0.6 is grid rounding and about -11.1 is five conduct moves. The large composite effect comes from the canonical integration premium: four dimensions fall from 4.0 to 3.8, which removes the 8-point bonus. Sensitivity check (canonical function): any one of A5, AC4, S2 or I4 alone yields 79.8 (Established); AB4 alone yields 81.8 (Exemplary). The band crossing survives rejection of any single move, and survives rejection of AB4 entirely. Confidence is medium: the placeholder base, a tier-5 release cited through verbatim republication (Beehive page unfetchable), and the full PDF not read. Proposed subdimensions cover every dimension whose raw value differs from the published vector (AWR, ACT, EQU, ACC, SYS, INT).

anti_false_positive_screening.baseline_provenance: No APPLIED_CHANGES entry, digest mention, prior assessment or proposal. 83.0 is the original placeholder; rotation-state last_assessed null.
anti_false_positive_screening.directionality: Surfaced on negative in-window evidence (Crown Review, 2 Sept); the proposal is a downgrade. Positive in-window conduct (apology, new monitoring role) credited.
anti_false_positive_screening.calibration_concern: Partly: the base is a placeholder. The crossing is NOT a grid artifact, though. Grid rounding alone gives 82.4 (still Exemplary); the crossing requires the conduct moves; any one of A5, AC4, S2 or I4 suffices (AB4 alone does not).
anti_false_positive_screening.allegation_vs_finding: The review is a statutory finding by a ministerially appointed team. It did not determine legal liability, and no legal liability is scored.
anti_false_positive_screening.attribution: Council owns the plant and holds the consent; only council governance conduct is scored. Wellington Water/Tiaki Wai and Veolia failures are not charged to the council except where the review assigns the council accountability.
